g.text: Windowed against temporal — two joins, two bounding mechanisms
windowed buffers up to 5 and waits · temporal enriches all 5 at once, 2 NULL
2 // Two of a row's five columns are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // key = which stream it is on: "a" = clicks, "b" = impressions
5 type Row { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 rows, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late impression
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: J — the join window, in seconds. J = 60
10 // primitive: LAG — each side's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the two sides. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: LEFT / RIGHT — the side names. LEFT = "a" · RIGHT = "b"
13 // primitive: rowsOf(key) — one side of the join.
15 // primitive: absDiff(a, b) — the distance between two times. absDiff(1, 50) = 49
16 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
17 // primitive: indexOf(r) — r's position in ARRIVAL order. indexOf(EVENTS[7]) = 7
21 // function: windowedJoin() — match two STREAMS within J. Bounded by TIME: the
22 // window bounds the buffer, and the watermarks bound the wait.
28 if (absDiff(l.et, r.et) <= J) { out = append(out, [l.id, r.id]) }
34 // function: tableAsOf(et) — the RIGHT side treated as a versioned TABLE: its
35 // state as it stood at that event time. NONE when no version existed yet.
49 // function: temporalJoin() — enrich each stream row from the table AS OF its own
50 // event time. Bounded by the TABLE: one lookup per row, no buffer, no wait.
60 // function: waitsFor(kind) — what each join is waiting on before it can emit.
67 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the same data, both joins.
Step 1/0 — the windowed join compares two STREAM rows
Both operands are stream rows, so neither is authoritative — the pair exists only if BOTH have arrived, which is why the buffer and the wait exist. 5 pairs
come out of this loop, and nothing here says when any of them may be published.

Step 2/0 — the temporal join probes a TABLE as of the row's own time
The `continue` skips table versions later than the row's own `et` — that is the "as of" semantics, and it is why the lookup needs the table's HISTORY rather
than its current value. For click 3 the answer is 11, determined the moment the click arrives.

Step 3/0 — so a row before the table existed gets NONE, not a wait
Click 0 at 12:00:01 precedes every impression, so `any` stays false and the result is NONE — **immediately**, not after a wait. Compare the windowed join,
where the same click's match with impression 7 requires a retraction to deliver.

Step 4/0 — and that is the whole difference: one waits, one does not
`wWaits` is "both watermarks" and `tWaits` is "nothing". Read the heap rows: `pairs` holds 5 matches of which 2 are never published, while `enriched` holds
all 5 rows, complete. Windowing a lookup imports the first column's problems for no benefit.
